\[
P(x) = \sum_{y} e^{-\lVert f(x) - f(y) \rVert^2 / (2 \sigma_k^2)},
\qquad
x \to \arg\min_{y : P(y) > P(x)} \lVert f(x) - f(y) \rVert
\]

The formula shows the default parameter values.

where

- \(f(x)\): The weighted color and the position of pixel x
- \(P(x)\): The density at pixel x
- \(\sigma_k\): The kernel size

f(x) holds the CIELAB color of pixel x, weighted by the color weight, and its position. The density P sums a Gaussian of the kernel size over the nearby pixels. Each pixel links to the nearest pixel with a higher density, so the links climb toward the peaks of the density. Links longer than the longest link are cut. The links that remain form trees, one per peak, and each tree is a region. Unlike mean shift, each pixel moves once, which makes it quick.
